newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-ZABEL STEPS UP TOUR CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-ZABEL STEPS UP TOUR CHALLENGE.

text.p: Germany's Erik Zabel stepped up his challenge for the Tour de France lead when he won the sixth stage over 217.5 kms from Le Blanc on Friday.

Zabel, who also won Tuesday's stage, edged out Dutchman Jeroen Blijlevens and Uzbekistan's Djamolidine Abdoujaparov to gain a 20-second bonus as stage winner. He also picked up 10 seconds bonus in intermediate sprints.
This cut the overall lead of Frenchman Cedric Vasseur to one minute and 49 seconds.
Vasseur and Zabel had to chase hard to rejoin the main field after the third crash of the day trapped them behind the fallers.
Italy's Mario Cipollini, who lost the yellow jersey to Vasseur on Thursday, also had to fight back from a crash but is still third overall, two minutes 15 seconds behind Vasseur.
After the first 77 kms the race took a 5-km detour to avoid a demonstration against nuclear waste dumping.
The riders also had to contend with headwinds and arrived some 30 minutes behind the slowest schedule.
